sum: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals reported strong third-quarter growth on Friday, October 30, while expanding its antibody alliance with Sanofi. The company also set dates for three upcoming healthcare investor conferences, keeping its pipeline and partnership strategy in focus for investors.

In its October 30 release, Regeneron said third-quarter revenue rose 36 percent year over year to 5.1 billion US dollars. GAAP diluted earnings per share increased 35 percent to 18.45 US dollars, while non-GAAP diluted earnings per share rose 70 percent to 20.07 US dollars.

Sanofi collaboration revenue reached 2.724 billion US dollars, supported by higher antibody profits and the full repayment of the Sanofi Development Balance in the second quarter. Regeneron said its expanded alliance with Sanofi covers four next-generation, long-acting antibodies. The company received a 1.0 billion US dollar upfront payment that it expects to recognize as collaboration revenue in the fourth quarter, with potential future milestones of up to 7.0 billion US dollars.

Regeneron announced on Monday, November 2, that management will participate in the Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London on November 17, the Evercore Healthcare Conference on December 1 and Citi's Global Healthcare Conference on December 2. The company announcement said the sessions will be webcast and that replays and transcripts will remain available for at least 30 days.

Regeneron stock traded at 811.60 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:00 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The quote provides a current trading reference, while the company's operating update and the expanded Sanofi relationship remain the principal business developments for the week.

Regeneron stock: Q3 revenue jumps 36% as Sanofi alliance expands
sum: Regeneron stock traded at 798.20 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 15:00 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The company is drawing investor attention after strong third-quarter growth and an expanded antibody alliance with Sanofi.

In its October 30 financial release, Regeneron said third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 36 percent from the year-earlier period to 5.116 billion US dollars. GAAP net income increased 33 percent to 1.949 billion US dollars, while diluted GAAP earnings per share rose 35 percent to 18.45 US dollars.

The quarter also marked a step-up in collaboration income. Sanofi collaboration revenue reached 2.724 billion US dollars, compared with 1.617 billion US dollars a year earlier. Regeneron attributed the increase primarily to its larger share of antibody commercialization profits and the full repayment of Sanofi's development balance in the second quarter.

Dupixent global net sales, recorded by Sanofi, rose 35 percent to 6.5 billion US dollars. Regeneron's EYLEA HD US sales increased 62 percent to 699 million US dollars, while global Libtayo sales rose 51 percent to 550 million US dollars. The product mix shows that collaboration income remains the largest near-term earnings driver, while growth in EYLEA HD and Libtayo supports the company's own commercial portfolio.

In October, Regeneron and Sanofi amended their antibody collaboration to add four Regeneron-invented, next-generation, long-acting antibodies. The companies will share development and commercialization costs equally and, if the programs reach the market, split global profits equally. Regeneron received a 1.0 billion US dollar upfront payment and is eligible for up to 7.0 billion US dollars in additional development, regulatory and sales milestones. Management expects to recognize the upfront payment as collaboration revenue in the fourth quarter.

Chief Executive Leonard Schleifer said the company has a pipeline of about 50 product candidates and highlighted continued progress in immunology, oncology, metabolic disease and rare disease. The company expects an FDA decision on cemdisiran for generalized myasthenia gravis in November 2026. Other disclosed milestones include planned data presentations in MASH and POTS during November and regulatory decisions for additional oncology applications in 2027.

sum: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals surged 13.33% to $927.89 on Friday, October 30, following third-quarter results that significantly beat estimates. Revenue rose 36% to $5.12 billion, and non-GAAP EPS jumped 70% to $20.07, driven by full Dupixent profit recognition from Sanofi and record sales across key drugs. The companies also expanded their alliance with a new $1 billion upfront deal. Technically, the stock exhibits strong bullish momentum with the RSI in overbought territory at 79. While a short-term pause is possible, a daily close above $930.46 targets $961.85, with key support at $870.49.

TradingKey - Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: REGN) jumped 13.33% to $927.89 on Friday, October 30, after third-quarter results beat estimates by a wide margin. It was the stock's highest close in at least a year, and it came on a day the S&P 500 fell 1.8%.

The key driver was Sanofi. Q3 was the first quarter Regeneron received its full share of Dupixent profits, after it finished repaying development costs that had been deducted from that share. The stock rose about 26% in October.

Revenue rose 36% to $5.12 billion, against about $4.58 billion expected, and non-GAAP EPS, which leaves out items such as stock-based pay, jumped 70% to $20.07, against an estimate of about $16.51, according to Trefis. GAAP EPS rose 35% to $18.45. CEO Leonard Schleifer called it "an outstanding quarter," with Dupixent, EYLEA HD and Libtayo each setting sales records.

Collaboration revenue from Sanofi rose 68% to $2.72 billion. Regeneron had been paying back its share of past development costs out of its Dupixent profits, and that balance was fully repaid at the end of Q2. From Q3 onward, the full profit share flows through, which makes this a lasting step-up rather than a one-time gain.
Dupixent, whose sales Sanofi records, grew 35% to $6.5 billion in the quarter, so the profit pool Regeneron shares in is still expanding.

In the US, EYLEA HD sales jumped 62% to $699 million, while the original EYLEA fell 41% to $400 million. Together, the two brought in about $1.1 billion, down only about 1% from a year earlier, with EYLEA HD now nearly two-thirds of the total. The higher-dose version is now offsetting most of the decline. Libtayo, Regeneron's cancer drug, rose 51% to $550 million.

Why Is Regeneron Stock Going Up?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) stock rose 13.3% on Friday, October 30, 2026, while the S&P 500 fell 1.8%. The advance occurred as Regeneron reported third-quarter 2026 results that topped analyst estimates for both earnings and revenue. By how much did Regeneron beat, and what was behind it?

Regeneron surpassed analyst estimates by a wide margin on both the top and bottom lines. The company posted adjusted earnings per share of $20.07 against an analyst estimate of $16.51, alongside revenue of $5.12 billion against a $4.58 billion estimate. Management said revenue grew 36% from a year earlier, mainly because of higher collaboration revenue from Sanofi, along with growth in Libtayo and EYLEA HD.

News reports linked the rise to EYLEA HD and to Regeneron’s Dupixent profits from Sanofi. Regeneron and Sanofi share the profits from a collaboration that includes Dupixent. Because Regeneron finished repaying a balance of development costs to Sanofi in the second quarter, management said the third quarter marked the first period the company recorded its full share of those profits.

That shift was visible in the figures. Regeneron’s share of the collaboration profits climbed 77% from a year earlier, an increase management put down mainly to Dupixent sales growth and the finished repayment. In total, collaboration revenue from Sanofi reached an all-time high of $2.7 billion.
EYLEA HD, part of Regeneron’s retinal franchise, generated U.S. sales of $699 million, up 62% from a year earlier. Even so, combined U.S. sales of EYLEA HD and EYLEA fell 1% over the same period.

Mostly, yes. Every company on Regeneron’s Trefis peer list advanced that session, logging gains that ranged from 1.1% for Amgen to 2.2% for Merck. XLV, the health care sector fund, added 0.5%. The wider market fell, and news reports tied that drop to selling in AI stocks after earnings from Amazon and Intel. None of the peers or the sector fund rose by more than 2.2%, so most of Regeneron’s gain was its own.

Regeneron stock: Q3 revenue jumps as Sanofi deal lifts outlook
sum: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals reported strong third-quarter results on Friday, October 30, with revenue and adjusted earnings benefiting from higher product sales and the full economic contribution of its Sanofi antibody alliance. The company said in a press release distributed by GlobeNewswire that third-quarter revenue reached USD 5.116 billion, while diluted GAAP earnings per share rose to USD 18.45.

Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share came in at USD 20.07, compared with USD 11.83 in the year-earlier quarter. GAAP net income increased to USD 1.949 billion from USD 1.460 billion. Regeneron said the quarter marked its third consecutive period of double-digit growth in revenue and non-GAAP earnings per share.

Sanofi collaboration revenue climbed to USD 2.724 billion from USD 1.617 billion. Regeneron said its development balance with Sanofi was fully repaid at the end of the second quarter, so the balance no longer reduced collaboration revenue in the third quarter. The company also said its share of profits from antibody commercialization rose to USD 2.575 billion.

The companies expanded their collaboration in October to include four Regeneron-invented, long-acting immunology antibodies. Regeneron received an upfront payment of USD 1.0 billion, with the potential for up to USD 7.0 billion in additional development, regulatory and sales milestones. The upfront payment is expected to be recognized as collaboration revenue in the fourth quarter.

EYLEA HD sales in the United States rose to USD 699 million from USD 431 million. Legacy EYLEA sales fell to USD 400 million from USD 681 million as patients continued to move toward the higher-dose product and competition weighed on demand. Combined US sales for the two products were broadly stable year over year.

Libtayo global sales increased to USD 550 million from USD 365 million. Dupixent global sales, recorded by Sanofi, reached USD 6.541 billion, up 35%. Regeneron also highlighted the FDA approval of Pasatru for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and said it expects a regulatory decision on cemdisiran in generalized myasthenia gravis next month.
Regeneron raised its 2026 ranges for research and development spending, while lowering its selling, general and administrative expense ranges.

sum: Regeneron (ISIN US75886F1075) was trading at EUR 698.45 at Lang & Schwarz on October 20, 2026 at 10:47 a.m. CEST. On October 12, 2026, Regeneron reported 84-week Pasatru results showing zero new heterotopic ossification lesions versus 9 for placebo.

The OPTIMA extension enrolled 63 adults, with 58 participants completing the double-blind extension phase to at least 84 weeks. The treatment groups also recorded 1 and 14 clinician-assessed flare-ups, compared with 17 for placebo, while skin and soft tissue infections occurred in 53 percent of the 3 mg/kg group and 78 percent of the 10 mg/kg group.

The result adds a late-stage rare-disease data point to Regeneron's broader development platform. The company said a Phase 3 trial in adolescents and children is planned to begin later in 2026, keeping execution and safety data central to the commercial outlook.

sum: A 4.89% slide to $729.05 takes roughly $3.6 billion off the biotech's market value in one session. Moves this size are rare for a $73.7 billion name, and the close is what matters now.
Regeneron slid to a $729.05 close, a decline of nearly 5% in a single session that is historically unusual for a company of this size.

Roughly $3.6 billion in market value evaporated in one day, a loss large enough to force institutional holders to reassess position sizes and risk exposure, which extends selling pressure beyond the initial session.

Pressure ran from the open onward, with the stock finding no meaningful floor until the final stretch of trading. A brief bounce around midday faded quickly, and the stock drifted back near session lows to close at $729.05.

For investors already holding shares, the closing price is the number that counts, since it sets the baseline for any recovery or further deterioration when trading resumes. A move of this magnitude warrants close attention to whether volume and price action stabilize or continue to lean negative in the sessions ahead.

sum: - Kodiak said its late-stage DAYBREAK study met its main goals: two candidates, including Zenkuda, matched Regeneron’s Eylea on vision after one year.
- 4D Molecular Therapeutics separately said the first patients had entered 4SIGHT, a late-stage trial of its one-time gene therapy 4D-150 in diabetic macular edema.
- Ocular plans to file for approval of its own wet AMD treatment AXPAXLI in the fourth quarter of 2026 and is preparing for a possible 2027 launch.

Shares of Ocular Therapeutix (OCUL) dropped more than 22% on Monday as investors reacted to upbeat late-stage results from two competitors targeting the same crowded market for longer-lasting wet age-related macular degeneration treatments.
The stock is now on track for its worst day since mid-February, if the losses hold. Eyepoint (EYPT) shares, another long-acting retina name, also traded 9% lower at the time of writing.

Kodiak Sciences (KOD) said its late-stage DAYBREAK study met its main goals. Two candidates, including Zenkuda, matched Regeneron’s Eylea on vision after one year. More than half of Zenkuda patients stayed on a six-month schedule under strict, real-world retreatment rules, and the company described a clean safety profile. Kodiak plans a multi-indication filing with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) later this year.

Wet age-related macular degeneration (Wet AMD) is an advanced eye disease where abnormal blood vessels grow under the retina and leak fluid into the macula, causing rapid central vision loss. While KOD stock more than doubled on the update, FDMT edged 2% lower.

REGN Deadline Alert: Levi & Korsinsky Reminds Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) Investors of Securities Class Action Deadline on September 14, 2026
sum: Important Notice Regarding Alleged Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo Clinical Trial Risk Misrepresentations. The lawsuit alleges Regeneron investors overpaid while the Company characterized slowing event accrual as potentially favorable, even as the study allegedly faced heightened risk of failing its primary endpoint.

NEW YORK, Sept. 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Levi & Korsinsky, LLP notifies investors in Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) that a class action lawsuit has been filed on behalf of shareholders who purchased securities between August 1, 2025 and May 15, 2026. Find out if you could qualify to recover your losses. You may also contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. at jlevi@levikorsinsky.com or (212) 363-7500.

Regeneron shares declined approximately 13.95%, or $102.09 per share, from the Class Period high through the final disclosure-related decline. Applications to serve as lead plaintiff must be filed by September 14, 2026.
The Alleged Clinical Trial Risk Securities Fraud Methodology

According to the lawsuit, Regeneron provided investors with materially positive information about the Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo Study while allegedly mischaracterizing the risk created by a prolonged slowdown in progression-free survival event accrual. The complaint alleges that investors were not told that preliminary statistical assumptions were flawed and that the trial was at increased risk of missing statistical significance.

The lawsuit contends that the Company framed the slowdown as consistent with durable efficacy in the active treatment arms, rather than as a warning sign that the study's statistical design and endpoint assumptions were under pressure.

The Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo Study tested a LAG-3 inhibitor combination as a first-line treatment for advanced melanoma. The complaint alleges that Regeneron's optimistic discussion of delayed event accrual caused investors to form expectations about the program that was not supported by the study's actual risk profile.

sum: Market impact notice: REGN shares allegedly lost $102.09 from the Class Period high after disclosures about a Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo protocol change and failed primary endpoint challenged earlier positive trial-risk messaging.

NEW YORK, Aug. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Levi & Korsinsky, LLP notifies investors in Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) that a class action has been filed on behalf of shareholders who purchased securities between August 1, 2025 and May 15, 2026. Find out if you may qualify to recover losses. You may also contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. at jlevi@levikorsinsky.com or (212) 363-7500.

REGN declined from $731.77 on April 28, 2026 to $629.68 after the May 15, 2026 after-market disclosure was reflected in trading, a $102.09 per-share drop, or approximately 13.95%. Investors seeking appointment as lead plaintiff must move the Court by September 14, 2026.
Market Impact From the Alleged Fianlimab-Libtayo Disclosure Shift

The securities action alleges that Regeneron and certain executives gave investors an overly positive view of the Phase III Fianlimab-Libtayo Study while minimizing the risk that slowing progression-free survival event accrual signaled statistical and clinical trial problems. The complaint contends that the market began repricing REGN shares after Regeneron disclosed on April 29, 2026 that the trial protocol had been altered to expand the patient population eligible for PFS analysis.

A second market reaction followed Regeneron's May 15, 2026 announcement that the Phase 3 trial did not reach statistical significance for the primary endpoint of improvement in PFS. The lawsuit asserts that these disclosures corrected earlier alleged misstatements and caused investors who purchased during the Class Period to suffer damages.
- REGN closed at $731.77 on April 28, 2026 before the protocol-change disclosure.

To own Regeneron, you need to be comfortable with a story built around high-value biologics, ongoing R&D spend, and managing the drag from a maturing EYLEA franchise. The latest quarter's higher revenue but softer earnings underscore how mix, pricing, and investment can pull in different directions, yet do not appear to change the central near term catalyst: how effectively Regeneron can defend and upgrade its ophthalmology business while offsetting competitive and pricing pressure on EYLEA.

The Telix collaboration on radiopharmaceutical oncology fits neatly beside this, as it extends Regeneron's oncology reach into precision radiotherapy rather than reshaping the near term profit picture. It looks more like a long term pipeline option that could complement existing biologics if it progresses, rather than a driver that alters current concerns around EYLEA competition, regulatory timing, and margin pressure in the next few quarters.
